extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for making and supporting rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (and related procedural instructions), plus introductory guidance on 35 U.S.C. 103 obviousness principles (KSR/Graham). Intended to instruct examiners which form paragraphs to use and the prerequisites/evidence required for each statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.06 (Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph must be used in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph only once in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.07.fti — Statement of Statutory Basis, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for rejections (e.g., 'A person shall be entitled to a patent unless—' ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute is no longer re-cited in all Office actions; it is required only in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Form paragraphs 7.07.fti to 7.14.fti are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action. For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to an application filed before that date, 7.07.fti must be preceded by form paragraph 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.08.fti — Pre-AIA 102(a): Activity by Another Before Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) the invention was known or used by others in this country, or patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country, before the invention thereof by the applicant for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.09.fti — Pre-AIA 102(b): Activity More Than One Year Prior to Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) the invention was patented or described in a printed publication ... or in public use or on sale in this country, more than one year prior to the date of application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti; may be preceded by 7.08.fti. When using 102(b) based on public use or sale, provide a full explanation of the evidence establishing the public use or sale (see form paragraph 7.16.fti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.10.fti — Pre-AIA 102(c): Invention Abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) he has abandoned the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti; may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08.fti and 7.09.fti. If used as a rejection, include a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment (see MPEP §2134 and form paragraph 7.17.fti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.11.fti — Pre-AIA 102(d): Foreign Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) the invention was first patented or caused to be patented ... in a foreign country prior to the date of the application for patent in this country on an application for patent or inventor’s certificate filed more than twelve months before the filing of the application in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti; may be preceded by form paragraphs 7.08.fti to 7.10.fti. When used as a rejection, include appropriate dates and explanation of how the foreign patent makes the reference available under 102(d) (see form paragraph 7.18.fti and MPEP §2135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12.fti — Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e): Patent Application Publication or Patent to Another with Earlier Filing Date (post-AIPA/AIPA rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) the invention was described in (1) an application for patent, published under section 122(b), by another filed in the United States before the invention by the applicant ... or (2) a patent granted on an application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention ... except that an international application filed under the treaty shall have the effects ... only if the international application designated the United States and was published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if the reference is: (a) a U.S. patent or publication of a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a); (b) a U.S. patent issued from, or a U.S. or WIPO publication of, an international application (PCT) if the international application has an international filing date on or after November 29, 2000; or (c) a U.S. patent issued from, or a WIPO publication of, an international design application that designates the U.S. Consider benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals under 119(e) and to nonprovisionals/international applications under 120/121/365(c)/386(c) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the earlier application(s). Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)-(d), 365(a)/(b), or 386(a)/(b). To rely on an international filing date under pre-AIA 102(e), the PCT must (1) be filed on or after Nov 29, 2000, (2) designate the U.S., and (3) have been published in English by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2); otherwise treat the reference under 102(a) or 102(b) as of its publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12.01.fti — Pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (PCT international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) the invention was described in a patent granted on an application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention ... — pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) applicable when reference is a U.S. patent resulting from an international application filed before Nov 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when the reference is a U.S. patent issued from a national stage of, or continuing application claiming benefit to, an international application having an international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000. Determine the reference's pre-AIPA 102(e) date as the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) were fulfilled for national stage patents; consider benefit claims to earlier-filed provisionals and nonprovisionals only if supported by the earlier disclosure; do NOT consider foreign priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.13.fti — Pre-AIA 102(f): Applicant Not the Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) he did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08.fti to 7.12.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.14.fti — Pre-AIA 102(g): Priority of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) during an interference another inventor establishes that before such person’s invention the invention was made by such other inventor and not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed; or (2) before such person’s invention the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it. Consider conception and reduction to practice dates and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08.fti to 7.13.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.fti — Rejection template for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a), (b), and (g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template: 'Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the appropriate paragraph letter(s) of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 in parentheses. In bracket 3 insert either '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with an explanation at the end of the paragraph. In bracket 4 insert the prior art relied upon. This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti and appropriate other paragraphs (7.08-7.14) or by form paragraph 7.103. If 102(e) is also applied, follow with the appropriate 7.15.01/7.15.02/7.15.03 form paragraph. For applications with filing date on/after March 16, 2013 claiming priority to earlier application, 7.06 must precede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.01.fti — Provisional rejection under pre-AIA 102(e) when copending application has common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are provisionally rejected under pre-AIA 102(e) as being anticipated by a copending application which has a common assignee, common applicant, or at least one common (joint) inventor. The provisional rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copending application must have a common assignee, applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), or at least one common (joint) inventor. The provisional rejection may be overcome by: a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of this application; or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131(a). It may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer. Use 7.12.fti to determine the copending application's 102(e) date unless the copending application is a national stage PCT with international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000 (then use 7.12.01.fti). If the claims would have been obvious over the copending application, use form paragraph 7.21.01.fti. If identical subject matter issues exist under 35 U.S.C. 101 or nonstatutory double patenting, use form paragraphs 8.30-8.39 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.02.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 102(e) when reference has common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) are rejected under pre-AIA 102(e) as being anticipated by [reference]. The applied reference has a common [assignee/applicant/joint inventor] with the instant application and, based upon its pre-AIA 102(e) date, constitutes prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when the patent or patent application publication is prior art under pre-AIA 102(e) and has a common assignee, applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), or joint inventor. Apply the rules of 7.12.fti (AIPA) or 7.12.01.fti (pre-AIPA) to determine the reference's 102(e) date. Consider benefit claims to earlier-filed provisionals/nonprovisionals only if supported in the earlier disclosure. Patent application publications may only be used if preceded by 7.12.fti. If the reference is a PCT publication with international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000, or that did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English, do not treat it as 102(e); instead apply 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.03.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 102(e) when no common assignee or inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) are rejected under pre-AIA 102(e) as being [clearly anticipated/anticipated] by [reference] where the patent or patent application publication has an earlier filing date and is not required to have a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.12.fti or 7.12.01.fti. Insert either '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with explanation. If the reference is a PCT publication with international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000, or if it did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English, do not treat as 102(e); apply 102(a) or (b) as of publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.16.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) for public use or on sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by either form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.09.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.17.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) for abandonment of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.10.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2 insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment. See MPEP §2134 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.18.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) for foreign patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants' [2]. [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.11.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 3 insert an explanation including appropriate dates and how they make the foreign patent available under 102(d). Refer to MPEP §2135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.19.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) when applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.13.fti or by paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2 insert an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP §2137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-claim and provisional-support rules for determining 102(e) dates
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining a reference’s pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date, consider benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), and to earlier-filed U.S. nonprovisional and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied upon earlier-filed application's disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 365(a)/(b), or 386(a)/(b). A reference is entitled to the benefit of a provisional filing date only if at least one of the claims in the reference is supported by the written description of the provisional application in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (35 U.S.C. 112(a)). See cited Federal Circuit decisions (Dynamic Drinkware; Amgen v. Sanofi) for precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT/international application publication conditions for being treated as 102(e) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: To rely on an international filing date for prior art purposes under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the international application (PCT) must have been filed on or after November 29, 2000, must have designated the U.S., and the international publication by WIPO must have been in English under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any condition is not met, the international application's publication may be applied under pre-AIA 102(a) or 102(b) as of its publication date. If a PCT was published in a language other than English or did not designate the U.S., the U.S. publication of the national stage (371) or a U.S. patent from the national stage may not be applied as 102(e) but may be applied under 102(a) or (b) as of publication date. Special rules apply for national-stage patents and continuing applications (see 7.12.01.fti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting and identical-subject-matter concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Two patents are not permitted to issue on identical subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 101; claims in the instant application directed to the same invention claimed in the reference should be provisionally rejected and the applicant required to amend or cancel claims so that both do not claim identical subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32 for provisional rejection of identical claims and form paragraph 8.27.fti to require amendment/cancellation; for subject matter not patentably distinct, reject on nonstatutory double patenting using form paragraph 8.33 and at least one of form paragraphs 8.34-8.39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness evaluation framework under 35 U.S.C. 103 (Graham/KSR guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Graham framework (scope and content of prior art; differences between claimed invention and prior art; level of ordinary skill; secondary considerations) and the flexible approach endorsed by the Supreme Court in KSR v. Teleflex. The KSR decision rejected a rigid application of the teaching-suggestion-motivation (TSM) test and emphasized a commonsense inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should: (1) not limit analysis to the specific problem the patentee identified; (2) recognize that a person of ordinary skill may be led to combine elements from prior art even if those elements addressed different problems; (3) consider 'obvious to try' in appropriate contexts; and (4) avoid rigid rules that deny recourse to common sense. However, invoking 'common sense' to supply a missing limitation must still be supported by evidence and a reasoned explanation, especially when the missing limitation goes to the heart of the invention (see Arendi v. Apple and other cited cases). For AIA-applicable cases use 'before the effective filing date of the claimed invention' as the relevant time; for pre-AIA use 'at the time of the invention.'
